A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EvolIF research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Material moved from v1's main text can be matched to v2's Appendices A–G; no essential comparison material is unavailable.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of ten LLMs, constraint-level results, patience experiments, thinking-mode comparisons, and synthesis-quality checks.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on 150 dialogues, including subjective constraints, sample-size sensitivity, query-quality audits, and system-prompt, synthesizer, and user-style analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds a style-conditioned query synthesis agent with topic and constraint checkers, iterative regeneration, and human review of unresolved queries (Section 3.2.2; Figure 2). v1 used direct LLM synthesis and explicitly left persona/style conditioning for future work. The underlying three-layer tracking mechanism remains.

E1.justification: The 541-topic seed pool and nine objective constraint groups remain, but v2 additionally evaluates emotion, writing-style, and target-age requirements. Queries now incorporate styles sampled from a pool derived from 500 personas (Section 4.1; Appendix B), substantially broadening response requirements and input conditions.

E2.justification: The main comparison replaces Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-4.1, and Mistral-Medium with Gemini-3.0-Pro, MiniMax-M2, and Mistral-Large-3 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 2). The system-prompt comparison also replaces GPT-5 and Grok-4-Fast with Gemini-3-Pro and Llama-4, retaining DeepSeek-V3.2.

E3.justification: The main evaluation expands from 50 to 150 dialogues and changes from GPT-4.1 synthesis to mixed GPT-4.1, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and DeepSeek-V3.1 synthesis. New protocols include subjective judging on a 1–10 scale with acceptance above 6 and sample-size comparisons from 30 to 150 dialogues. ACT/LSS renaming alone preserves the metric formulas.

E4.justification: v2 adds sample-size stability analysis, checker-quality audits, synthesizer correlations, and formal-versus-informal user-style analysis (Section 5.5; Appendices C, F, G). System-prompt and synthesizer analyses are revised. v1's Grok-4-Fast thinking-mode study is removed, while constraint-difficulty and patience analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 adds Pearson correlations for sample-size stability and Spearman correlations across synthesizers (Table 4; Figure 6). Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, seeds, or repeated-evaluation run counts. The new k = 3 setting concerns query-regeneration attempts, not repeated evaluation runs.

E6.justification: Main, constraint-level, and ablation results are extensively replaced or expanded. GPT-5's reported raw duration and ROB change from 18.54 turns and 70.31% to 19.32 turns and 66.40% (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 2), under different benchmark conditions. New subjective, sample-size, and style results appear; thinking-mode results disappear.

T1.justification: Most mathematics remains equivalent under ACT/LSS-to-EDR renaming. Appendix A.2 adds endurance-range reasoning. However, v2 Equation 3 decrements patience on success, reversing v1 Equations 7–8 and contradicting v2's surrounding failure-based description. This changes the printed mathematics without establishing a change to implemented termination.

C1.justification: The central extensible-benchmark and patience-based evaluation contributions remain. v2 foregrounds the checked synthesis agent and Flow Theory and expands the benchmark's claimed coverage. Its headline GPT-5 duration shifts from 18.54 raw turns to approximately 14 successful turns, and the headline comparator becomes Gemini-3.0-Pro.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning textual scope, LLM judging, and family bias (Section 7). It qualifies age-related failures as potentially reflecting judge disagreement and acknowledges style confounding in synthesizer comparisons. System-prompt benefits are narrowed after Llama-4 improves without one; v1's thinking-versus-formatting interpretation is removed.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C add annotator roles, topic/keyword verification, persona-to-style construction, checker operation, and subjective-judge scoring details; Section 4.1 specifies three regeneration attempts. v2 also replaces v1's future code/data-release promise with stated resource availability and a repository link, materially expanding documented reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Flow Theory, persona generation, emotion/style/age constraints, Arena-Hard judging, and judge-family bias. These extend the framework's motivation and implementation grounding, while the related-work taxonomy and positioning against existing instruction-following benchmarks remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods, and results are extensively condensed and rewritten. Basic metric explanations and detailed analyses move into appendices, a separate Limitations section appears, and ACT/LSS terminology becomes EDR variants. The author list and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with styles, checkers, and human review; constraint tables and radar plots expand to twelve groups. v2 removes the thinking-mode figure, adds a correlation heatmap and style chart, compresses the patience table to one metric per threshold, and splits or relocates several existing displays.

improvement.justification: The mixed-synthesizer main evaluation, sample-size checks, documented validation workflow, and explicit judge limitations strengthen reliability assessment and transparency relative to v1. The net gain is limited by new reporting errors: Equation 3 reverses the patience condition, and Table 7 reports successful-turn counts exceeding partial-credit endurance, contradicting the metric definitions.
